_comment: Hand-edited: topicMap, map, short, exclude, notes, domains. Everything else is generated by sync.mjs from the GitHub API — do not hand-edit entries/stack/tests/lastPush/synced.

domains.name: ASSURANCE
domains.chasing: What I am chasing here: the smallest honest evidence set that proves a control operates.
domains.empty: Nothing here yet. When something ships, it appears on the chart on its own.

domains.name: ENGINEERING
domains.chasing: Security work only counts once it runs unattended. This row is the difference between an opinion and a tool.

domains.name: DETECTION
domains.chasing: A control you cannot observe failing is a control you are trusting on faith.

domains.name: APPSEC
domains.note: secure sdlc / code review / supply chain
domains.chasing: Most of what breaks applications is authorisation and trust in things you did not write.

domains.name: CLOUD
domains.chasing: The gap between what a cloud provider promises, what a framework asks for, and what the policy actually permits.

domains.name: OFFENSIVE
domains.chasing: Offence here exists to validate the defensive work above, not as a separate hobby.

domains.name: AI SECURITY
domains.chasing: The novel part is not the model. It is what loading an artifact, or composing a toolset, quietly grants.

SecureBridge-ISMS-360.tag: a whole ISMS, end to end
SecureBridge-ISMS-360.readFirst: The risk register and the control-to-evidence mapping.
SecureBridge-ISMS-360.why: Most GRC examples show one control. This shows the system they live in.

AegisLens-security-workbench.tag: evidence in, risk scored, report out
AegisLens-security-workbench.readFirst: `backend/tests` — if you want to know whether I can actually build.
AegisLens-security-workbench.why: The tooling half of the SecureBridge problem.

PingMaster.why: The first half of every detection story is seeing the traffic at all.

TrustEdge-AWS-IAM-analyzer.tag: who outside your AWS account can get inside it
TrustEdge-AWS-IAM-analyzer.readFirst: The trust-policy grading logic — that is where the argument is.
TrustEdge-AWS-IAM-analyzer.why: An IAM trust policy is a door. Whoever gets through it holds real AWS credentials.
TrustEdge-AWS-IAM-analyzer.runs: Offline. No credentials, no API calls, nothing leaves the machine.

BlackOut.tag: one control failure, followed all the way through
BlackOut.readFirst: The exploit, then the detection rule written against it.
BlackOut.why: An authorisation fail-open taken from exploit to root cause to fix to detection rule to regression test. The whole loop, not just the finding.

NullFire.tag: the Sigma rules that can never fire
NullFire.readFirst: The matchability analysis — why a rule is dead against your real data.
NullFire.why: A detection rule that cannot match anything is worse than no rule: it looks like coverage.

Pedigree-npm-provenance-gate.tag: where did this dependency actually come from
Pedigree-npm-provenance-gate.readFirst: The dry-run report — what would break if you enforced the policy today.
Pedigree-npm-provenance-gate.why: Verifies origin, not the absence of malicious code. Being clear about what it does not prove is the point.

sunset.tag: what breaks when the cryptography expires
sunset.readFirst: The triage output - especially the section listing what it could not assess.
sunset.why: Turns a CycloneDX CBOM into a deadline-anchored migration plan for post-quantum cryptography.

spectre-ssrf-lab.readFirst: The bypass techniques, then the detection rules written against them.
spectre-ssrf-lab.why: A self-contained SSRF research lab. Every scenario is reproducible on 127.0.0.1, which is the only responsible way to publish this.

AfterLife.tag: the password reset worked; the attacker stayed
AfterLife.readFirst: The naive detection rule that misses it - that contrast is the point.
AfterLife.why: Reproduces a real conditional-revocation bug (Strapi CVE-2026-22706) end to end: the flaw, its fix, a three-rule detection pack, and the rule that looks right but fails.

credscope.tag: what the credential can actually do
credscope.readFirst: The blast-radius scoring — a key is only as interesting as its reach.
credscope.why: Non-human identity attack surface. Machine credentials outnumber human ones and nobody reviews them.

sleeper.readFirst: Where reach and detectability disagree — that gap is the finding.
sleeper.why: OAuth grant drift, with reach scored independently of whether you would notice it being used.

tombstone.readFirst: A field where the retention floor and the erasure obligation cannot both be met.
tombstone.why: Security telemetry must be kept; privacy law says delete it. This works out field by field whether deletion is technically achievable at all.

deadweight.tag: what happens when you load the model
deadweight.readFirst: The pickle analysis — it answers the question without ever executing the artifact.
deadweight.why: AI model and skill supply-chain analysis. Loading an artifact is code execution, and most tooling treats it as data.

handler.tag: what a toolset can do in combination
handler.readFirst: The minimal change that breaks the capability path.
handler.why: Individual agent tools look harmless. Composition is where the capability appears, and that is what this attributes.

parallax.tag: numbers that cannot carry the decision
parallax.readFirst: The triage — which few risks are actually worth quantifying.
parallax.why: A qualitative risk register produces numbers people then make decisions on. This finds where those numbers cannot bear the weight.
